entries.notes:
# v1.3.41 — reader progress line reset, account level on read

- Fixed: the reader's progress line stayed full at the end of a chapter and did
  not reset when the next chapter began. It now rewinds to the start of each new
  chapter — including chapters loaded automatically as you reach the end of one —
  and follows the chapter you are actually reading as you scroll.
- Fixed: your account level did not increase after reading a chapter. The level
  and the "N chapters to Lv N+1" counter now update from your chapters read on
  this device, and a level earned on another device is never lowered.

# v1.3.40 — reader sheet iOS polish, fixed chapter count and chapter list

- Improved: the reader settings sheet now reads like iOS Settings. The sheet
  title is centered, Reading Mode uses text-only segments, Focus Mode uses a
  standard iOS toggle, and chapter nav, Return to Details, engine status pills
  and the theme swatches all follow the same equal-width iOS rows.
- Fixed: the chapter count is now bold and correct in both the reading bar and
  the Chapters header of the settings sheet. It counts from the first chapter,
  so Chapter 1 of a 23-chapter title shows `1 / 23` instead of `23 / 23`.
- Improved: the chapter picker and the settings-sheet Chapter dropdown now list
  chapters oldest-first, with Chapter 1 at the top. The chapter picker marks the
  current chapter with an iOS check instead of the old "Last read" text.
- Fixed: the chapter list no longer draws a lighter box behind each row, and
  long chapter titles now wrap to fit inside the sheet instead of overflowing.

# v1.3.39 — simpler reader sheet, a chapter dropdown, and a cleaner reading bar

- New: the reader settings sheet is rebuilt to match iOS Settings — grouped inset
  cards, one clear list, no clutter. The Performance option now sits with Display,
  chapter navigation is a clean chevron row, and the desktop-only keyboard
  shortcuts footer is gone.
- New: pick any chapter right from the settings sheet. A new Chapter dropdown
  lists every chapter and jumps straight to the one you choose, without leaving
  the reader.
- Improved: the reading bar is simpler. The zoom buttons, translate button,
  settings gear and read-aloud button are removed, leaving Back, the chapter
  title, Chapters and Quick settings. The full settings sheet opens from
  "All Settings" in the quick-settings sheet.
- Fixed: the settings sheet no longer falls off the bottom of the screen on
  Android. It now sizes to the dynamic viewport and reserves the system
  navigation inset, so every option stays reachable.

# v1.3.38 — reader sheet fixes, detail skeletons, mgeko chapter labels

- Fixed: the reader's quick-settings and chapter sheets could not be closed.
  They now close by tapping the backdrop, dragging the panel down, tapping the
  new bottom handle bar, or pressing Escape, and they slide up when they open.
- New: swipe up from the bottom of the reading screen to open the quick-settings
  sheet, without leaving the page you are reading.
- New: the title detail page now shows shimmer placeholders for the author line
  and the genre tags while the source loads, instead of "Loading..." or nothing.
- Fixed: mgeko chapters no longer show the "-eng-li" language tag — a chapter
  now reads "Chapter 1" instead of "1-eng-li".

# v1.3.37 — App Store reading bar, chapter picker and quick settings

- New: the reader's top bar is rebuilt in the App Store style — a frosted bar with
  SF-style icons, a centered chapter title and a chapter position subtitle.
- New: pick any chapter without leaving the reader. A new Chapters button opens an
  iOS inset list of every chapter with your current chapter marked.
- New: a quick-settings sheet from the reading bar — reading mode, brightness,
  auto-scroll and speed in one compact iOS panel, with a shortcut to all settings.
- Fixed: the reader now reliably tells novels apart from manga/manhwa/manhua from
  the title's content type, so novel-only controls (novel display options, read
  aloud) never appear for comics, and comic-only controls never appear for novels.

# v1.3.36 — account level now matches the cloud

- Fixed: the level shown on the Account screen could disagree with your
  account. The big level badge was derived only from the reading log on this
  device, so a device whose log lagged behind (for example after a reinstall or
  a restored backup) showed a lower level than the cloud. The badge now reflects
  your account's level, and falls back to the on-device level only when you are
  signed out.
- Fixed: opening the Account screen now pulls your latest cloud progress once
  per session, so bookmarks, history and chapter reads from your other devices
  appear on this one without a manual sync.
- Fixed: syncing can no longer lower your account level. A device with fewer
  local chapter reads than the account keeps the higher cloud level instead of
  overwriting it.

# v1.3.35 — multi-provider coverage + a compact source picker

- New: titles now list every provider that carries them. Home, Latest and
  search results are interleaved across sources and the backend waits for all
  providers (bounded to 6 s) instead of stopping after the first few, so a
  title shows all of its available sources instead of just one.
- Fixed: the detail page's source enrichment no longer times out. Opening a
  title that was listed with a single source now fills in the other providers
  within a few seconds.
- New: the App Store-style detail page shows the Sources picker as a compact
  dropdown — a single row with the active source and a chevron that opens a
  floating menu listing every provider, with a check on the active one.

# v1.3.34 — detail page: no more sideways scroll, skeleton loading, single source row

- Fixed: on a phone the title detail page could be swiped left and right. An
  over-wide action bar (the auto-download toggle) pushed the page wider than the
  screen. The auto-download toggle has been removed from the detail page, and
  the detail view now clips horizontal overflow so the page can never pan
  sideways. The auto-download feature itself is unchanged and still works for
  titles that already have it enabled.
- New: the detail page's Information card (Source, Type, Status, Author, Artist,
  Chapters) and the About blurb now show shimmer skeleton placeholders while the
  source loads, instead of dashes and a "Loading description..." label.
- Fixed: the Sources list on the detail page no longer shows the same provider
  twice. Sources are collapsed to one row per provider.

# v1.3.33 — App Store detail page, chapter upload dates, library cleanup, search rework

- New: the title detail view is now a full Apple App Store product page for the
  App Store themes. It has a sticky frosted nav bar with Back and Share, a
  centered hero cover, an iOS Information card, a clamped About section with
  more/less, an iOS Sources inset list, clean chapter rows with a Select mode
  and a long-press action sheet, and a sticky call-to-action bar.
- New: chapter upload dates. A shared `public/js/chapter-date.js` normalizes
  ISO, epoch and human dates across providers and renders a friendly label
  (Today, Yesterday, Nd ago, Nw ago, Nmo ago) in both chapter renderers.
- Removed: the Library category system. The Plan to Read, Reading, Completed
  and Dropped chips, the smart-category derivation, plan-to-read reminders, the
  detail category dropdown and the category-edit modal are all gone.
- Improved: the bookmark button now shows an outline or filled bookmark icon
  alongside its label.
- Improved: the Library search is fully App Store themed with an iOS field, a
  Cancel button and a no-match state, and the white toolbar slab behind the
  search has been removed.

# v1.3.32 — library integrity, local API hardening, Indonesian sources

- Fixed: your library, history and stats could come back empty after a crash or
  a kill mid-write. The database is now written atomically (temp file, fsync,
  then rename) and checked for integrity when it opens; a corrupt file is
  quarantined and a fresh one is created instead of the app silently serving an
  empty library. A one-time, idempotent migration also removes leftover
  test-fixture rows.
- Fixed: real series with a 1-character title no longer disappear from the
  Library, History and Stats, and are no longer dropped on import, merge or
  export. The old rule treated any 1-character title as a placeholder. Backup
  import now reports the rows it skips instead of dropping them silently.
- Security: the local loopback API now requires a per-install token on every
  route that writes data, so an unrelated local process can no longer inject
  junk into your library. The token is injected into the served page and echoed
  back by the app automatically.
- New: three Indonesian sources — MangaIndo, Komikindo and Bacakomik.
- Fixed: the Android boot entry point called an undefined `formatError`, which
  crashed the boot handler and hid the real error behind a generic failure.

# v1.3.31 — Robust update check on launch + persistent sign-in

- Fixed: the update check could be skipped entirely when the embedded local
  server was slow to start — it was awaited inside the same try as the server
  readiness check, so a readiness failure swallowed it. The check now always
  runs at launch and, when an update exists, shows a dismissible banner on the
  Home screen (View opens the changelog; dismissing remembers that version).
- Fixed: you were signed out once the 24-hour session token aged out. Sessions
  now renew automatically on activity, so an active account stays signed in
  indefinitely and only ~30 days of total inactivity asks you to sign in again.

# v1.3.30 — Rankings spread across the full provider pool

- Fixed: the Top Charts / leaderboard was dominated by a single provider —
  whichever source won the fetch race filled nearly the whole page. Rankings
  now draw evenly from the full provider pool, so results are spread across
  many sources.

# v1.3.29 — Home skeleton loading + skeleton shimmer theme fix

- Improvement: Home now shows shimmering skeleton placeholders while Rankings,
  Recommendations and Continue Reading load, instead of blank or absent
  sections — so the layout no longer jumps while those dynamic sections resolve.
- Fixed: skeleton shimmer was invisible in the dark and light themes; the
  placeholder colours were only defined for the App Store themes.

# v1.3.28 — detail provider-menu race fix + broader leaderboard sources

- Fixed: opening a title and rapidly switching to another no longer shows the
  previous title's source list. Stale background lookups from an earlier title
  are discarded instead of overwriting the current detail view.
- Improvement: Top Charts / leaderboard now draws on the full provider pool
  (bounded by a 6-second deadline) instead of stopping at the first few
  responders, so more sources appear.

# v1.3.27 — OTA update UI: progress bar, install phases, restart prompt

- New: app updates now show real byte-level download progress. The install
  streams from the server and the Updates panel (and the changelog modal) show a
  true percentage bar with the downloaded/total MB as the bundle arrives, rather
  than a static "Downloading..." label.
- New: an install phase checklist walks through Download → Verify → Install →
  Restart. The current step spins while it runs and each finished step gets a
  checkmark, so it is clear what the update is doing.
- New: an update-available banner appears in the Updates panel and at the top of
  the changelog modal, showing the new version, the download size, the release
  date and an Install action.
- New: the changelog list is polished with a version chip, a "Latest" badge on
  the newest entry, and human-friendly relative dates (today / yesterday /
  N days ago).
- New: after an update installs, a restart prompt offers "Restart Now" or
  "Later". Choosing "Later" leaves a persistent reminder in the Updates panel
  until the app is actually restarted.
- Fixed: the `hidden` helper now hides and shows the new update panels
  correctly — the OTA elements use scoped `.hidden` rules instead of a global
  rule that would have clobbered the navigation slide-out and scroll-indicator
  fades.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.26 — Hide test-fixture entries

- Fixed: leftover test/diagnostic entries (for example "E2E History",
  "Diag History" and "Drag History", plus the earlier "T" stubs) no longer
  appear in your History or Library. These came from old automated test runs.
- The app now recognises fixture entries by their title prefix and by the
  test-only sources they use, and filters them out everywhere — in History, in
  the Library, in your reading stats, and when syncing — so they are never
  shown and never uploaded to your account.
- Real titles are unaffected: a genuine series such as "Dragon Ball",
  "Dragonslayer" or "Testament of Sister New Devil" is still shown normally.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.25 — Ignore placeholder entries

- Fixed: junk "placeholder" entries — a bookmark or history item whose title is a
  single character such as "T" — no longer appear in your Library or History.
  Some leftover cloud test data contained these stubs, which showed up as a "T"
  series duplicated many times.
- The app now filters these placeholders everywhere: when loading your Library
  and History, when importing a backup, when merging cloud data, and when
  syncing — so they never render and are never re-uploaded to your account.
- Your real bookmarks and reading history are untouched.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.24 — Account sign-in panel skeleton

- New: when you first open the Account tab, the Account (sign-in) panel now
  shows shimmer placeholders while your sign-in state loads, instead of
  briefly flashing the sign-in form. It then reveals "Signed in as …" with
  your level, or the sign-in form if you are signed out.
- The placeholder appears only on the first load of the Account tab per
  session; later refreshes (signing in or out, syncing) update silently with
  no skeleton flash.
- If the account service cannot be reached, the placeholder is cleared and the
  panel falls back to its normal content — nothing is left shimmering.
- Fixed: the account panel's data now finishes loading before the shimmer is
  removed, so the sign-in state no longer appears a moment after the skeleton
  disappears.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.23 — Account tab skeleton loading

- New: the Account tab now shows shimmer skeleton placeholders over the three
  data regions while your stats load for the first time in a session — the hero
  (rank / level / progress), Chapter Milestones (badge grid, streak chips, goal
  values) and Reading Stats (the stat cards, the 14-day sparkline, and the Top
  Sources / Top Genres breakdowns).
- The skeleton appears only on the first load. Re-opening the tab, or any later
  refresh (saving a goal, clearing history, restoring a backup, changing the
  naming theme), updates the values silently with no skeleton flash.
- If a stats load fails, the skeleton is cleared and the previous placeholder
  text returns, so nothing is left shimmering.
- The Account, Appearance, Performance, Content, Data & Backup, Diagnostics and
  Updates panels stay interactive immediately and are not covered by the
  skeleton.
- No other behaviour changed.

# v1.3.22 — Mgeko source back online

- Fixed: the Mgeko source returned no results and reported a TLS/certificate
  error. The cause was not an expired certificate on Mgeko itself — it was local
  network DNS interference returning the wrong server for the Mgeko host, which
  made the secure connection fail. Mgeko's host is now resolved correctly, so
  search, popular listings, details and chapters work again, with full
  certificate validation preserved.
- Fixed: Mgeko cover images hosted on the same affected host now load again
  through the image proxy.
- Note: this is a network-resolution fix only; nothing about your library or
  reading progress changes.

# v1.3.21 — stay signed in when the sync server is offline

- Fixed: if the sync server (the Raspberry Pi behind the account gateway) goes
  offline, you are no longer signed out. The app keeps your session and shows
  your account as before, then syncs normally once the server is reachable
  again.
- Fixed: a server outage is no longer reported as a wrong password. Trying to
  sign in while the server is unreachable now shows an honest "can't reach the
  sync server" message instead of an incorrect "invalid credentials" error.
- Note: your reading progress and library always stay on the device, so an
  offline server never costs you anything locally.

# v1.3.20 — loading feedback on account buttons

- New: the Sync Now, Create Account and Sign In buttons now show a spinning
  loading ring while the app is working, so it is clear the tap registered and
  something is happening.
- New: all of those buttons press in with a subtle scale animation on tap,
  matching the rest of the app's motion. The press animation is disabled when
  the system "reduce motion" setting is on.
- The button's label is preserved while loading and the button returns to its
  normal state as soon as the action finishes, whether it succeeds or fails.

# v1.3.19 — sync no longer reports the Pi as unreachable

- Fixed: syncing a large library no longer fails with "pi_unreachable". The
  sync used to upload your entire library in one request, which took longer
  than the account gateway's timeout, so a sync that was actually succeeding
  was reported as a failure. Progress is now uploaded in small batches, so
  each request finishes quickly and the sync completes reliably.
- Fixed: chapter-read entries are now written in the field names the account
  backend expects, so reads sync correctly instead of being silently rejected.
- Fixed: a brand-new account's level is no longer sent as 0 (which the backend
  rejected); it is clamped to 1 so the profile save succeeds.
- Note: your reading progress was never lost — it was always written on the
  device. This release makes the cloud copy actually complete.

# v1.3.18 — professional legal documents, sign-in animation, account sync on sign-in

- New: the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy are rewritten as full,
  professional documents. They now render as a properly formatted document in
  the legal modal — headings, lists and emphasis — instead of showing raw
  markdown markers like `##` and `**`.
- New: the sign-in gate animates in with a subtle, App Store-style sequence. The
  card, fields, consent rows and buttons fade and rise in turn, inputs get a
  focus ring, buttons press in, and error messages shake. All of the motion
  honours the system "reduce motion" setting.
- Fixed: signing in or creating an account now syncs the account with the
  reading progress already on the device. Previously a fresh account could show
  0 bookmarks, 0 history and level 0 even though the device held a full library;
  the app now pushes the local progress up and refreshes your level right after
  sign-in, with a toast reporting the synced counts.

# v1.3.17 — boot-screen hotfix for the v1.3.16 security update

- Fixed: the Android app could hang forever on the boot/loading screen after
  the v1.3.16 security update. The boot screen polls the local server's
  readiness status, but the hardening had removed the cross-origin header that
  read required, so the WebView blocked the response, the retry never fired and
  the app never advanced past the loading page. The server now allows that one
  read-only readiness check again while every sensitive endpoint stays locked
  down exactly as before.
- Fixed: the local server now answers on both IPv4 and IPv6 loopback, so
  `localhost` resolves and connects on all devices. Some Android WebViews prefer
  the IPv6 address, which the previous IPv4-only bind did not cover.

# v1.3.16 — mandatory sign-in gate and security hardening

- New: the app now requires sign-in before use. On first launch you must accept
  the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy, and the acceptance is recorded
  before any library data is shown. The legal documents ship with the app, so
  the gate works offline.
- Security: removed the wildcard CORS policy. The local API is unauthenticated,
  so a permissive `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` let any web page read your
  bookmarks, history and backups from `localhost`. Every legitimate client is
  same-origin, so the browser now blocks cross-origin reads by default. A
  same-site guard additionally rejects cross-site `POST`s to destructive
  routes, and the heavy endpoints (OTA install/rollback/restart, cache clear,
  server restart, user import) get a much tighter rate limit.
- Security: the image proxy now rejects non-http(s) schemes and private,
  loopback, link-local and reserved hosts, including names that merely resolve
  to them, and caps a single proxied image at 8 MB so the unauthenticated
  endpoint cannot be used as an unbounded bandwidth pump.
- Security: provider content is HTML-escaped and sanitised before it is
  rendered. Cover URLs, titles, authors, statuses and descriptions are escaped,
  and the remote changelog/release-notes markdown is reduced to an allow-list of
  inert formatting tags (links keep only `http(s)` hrefs).
- Security: pinned the `marked` CDN script with a Subresource Integrity hash so
  a tampered or replaced CDN payload is refused by the browser.
- Security: the service worker no longer caches personal API responses
  (`/api/user/`, `/api/logs`, `/api/ota/`, `/api/download/`). Those routes carry
  per-user data or one-shot update payloads, so a cached copy could leak between
  sessions or serve stale personal state; they now go straight to the network.
- Changed: the client-side password rule is raised to a minimum of 12
  characters, matching the account backend, so registration no longer passes the
  local check only to fail with `weak_password`.

# v1.3.15 — optional cloud sync through the Vercel↔Pi connector

- New: a second, fully optional cloud-sync path through the Vercel↔Pi
  connector gateway. It uses bearer-token auth over a cross-origin
  connection, and when it is configured it takes precedence over the direct
  PocketBase backend.
- The Account panel gains this second backend transparently — there is no UI
  change, and sign-in and sync keep working exactly as before when the
  connector is not configured.
- Fixed: **Sync Now** now surfaces real errors instead of reporting a false
  success when a sync request fails, so you can tell when something went
  wrong.
- Note: cloud features stay fully optional. With no backend URL configured the
  app remains local-first and the Account panel simply shows
  "Not configured".

# v1.3.14 — accounts + level badges + cloud sync

- New: an **Account** panel in the Account view lets you create an account or
  sign in with email + password, and sync your reading progress to the cloud.
- New: a numeric **level** now sits alongside your rank. You gain a level
  every ~10 chapters (level 1 at 0, level 2 at 10 chapters, level 5 at 100,
  level 10 at 500), and the Account hero shows a Level + XP progress bar with
  "N chapters to Lv N+1".
- Changed: each milestone badge's sub-label now shows the **level** it
  unlocks (e.g. `Lv 5`) instead of the raw chapter count (`100 ch`).
- Sync: **Sync Now** merges your local library with the cloud
  (last-write-wins per row, chapter reads unioned) so progress carries across
  devices. Signing out keeps everything local.
- Note: cloud features stay fully optional — with no Supabase keys configured
  the app remains local-first and the Account panel simply shows
  "Not configured".

# v1.3.13 — reader keep-awake + brightness dimmer

- New: a **Keep Awake** switch in the reader's Display settings holds the
  screen on while a chapter is open, so long chapters no longer time out
  mid-scroll. It is opt-in and defaults to off, so an untouched install
  behaves exactly as before.
- New: a **Brightness** slider dims the reader page on its own, down to 80%
  black, without dragging the toolbar or the settings sheet down with it. It
  defaults to 0% (no dimming).
- Both settings persist across chapters and app restarts, and the reader
  releases the wake flag and resets the dimmer when it closes.
- Note: the wake lock is applied on device through the native Android bridge
  (`setKeepScreenAwake`), so keep-awake is Android-only; the brightness dimmer
  works everywhere.

# v1.3.12 — memory pressure, downloads label, IPv4-first networking

- Fix: the app was being killed by Android on memory-constrained devices. The
  proxied-image cache is now bounded by total bytes (32MB) instead of a raw
  item count, so a few large images can no longer blow past the intended
  budget.
- Fix: the Android reader preload window is smaller, cutting peak memory while
  scrolling through image-heavy chapters.
- Fix: the Downloads screen no longer shows a raw "CANCELLED" row — cancelled
  downloads are hidden and every remaining status has a friendly label.
- Fix: updates and providers could time out on networks that advertise IPv6
  but do not route it. The Android runtime now resolves IPv4 first, so the OTA
  feed and providers are reachable again.
- Note: the Android networking fix no longer enables Happy Eyeballs
  (autoSelectFamily) — it crashed on Node 18 with an internal assertion, so the
  IPv4-first DNS ordering is applied on its own.
- Scope: the networking and preload changes apply to the Android runtime; the
  cache byte budget and downloads labels apply everywhere.
